runs.content: Wednesday's rotation deep-dives Health + Learning. Both domains are quiet — unchanged since 2026-05-15, no new source material in either since the last Health/Learning-focus run (2026-09-09), and nearly every major gap between them and the rest of the wiki is already logged from prior runs (Health goals stub, my-protocol empty, Ferriss fear-setting, creatine dosing, cognitive-stimulation/games, breathwork/Little Ninja, Seth Godin and Tim Ferriss cross-domain bridges, book-breath cross-link). Deep-read the previously-undived Learning framework pages (empathy-worldview, enrollment, Dave Gray's empathy map, Kevin Kelly's 1,000 True Fans) for a fresh angle instead of re-covering the same ground. Found one: learning/framework-empathy-worldview.md's own 'Applied to Business / Crypto / AI' section gives an explicit diagnostic — when something isn't being adopted, ask what the resister believes/wants/knows that makes non-adoption the rational choice, not why they're being irrational — but it's never been tested against real material. ai-tech/data-ai-enterprise-adoption-economist-2026-06-27.md (an older AI & Tech page, not previously deep-dived) is exactly that material: Natura's CDO's 'I have a Ferrari but I don't have the driver' quote, and the report's own Finding #5 ('the hardest part... is not building the models but rewiring the organisation'), describe stalled AI adoption entirely as a training/ROI-sequencing problem, never naming the possibility that resisting employees hold a rational worldview (job-loss fear, distrust of unaudited AI decisions) — precisely the question the Learning framework was built to ask. The two pages are five weeks apart in creation and have never been linked. Concrete next step: cross-link data-ai-enterprise-adoption-economist-2026-06-27.md's Finding #5 to framework-empathy-worldview.md's belief/want/know diagnostic, both ways. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-22.

Tuesday's rotation deep-dives AI & Tech + Technology. No new source material had landed in either domain since the last AI-Tech-focus run (2026-09-15, the Kakashii ingest) — today's clippings-sorter batches were all Finance-domain — so instead of re-covering already-flagged pages, deep-read ai-tech-overview.md, technology/overview.md, and a handful of older, previously-undived AI & Tech source pages for a fresh angle. Found one: ai-tech/source-uptime-ai-efficiency-metrics-2026.md (Uptime Institute, Jan 2026) and finance/investor-letters/source-burry-ap-sbc-tragic-algebra-2026-04-07.md run the identical analytical move in two different domains — an industry converging on a flattering headline metric (AI chips' 4-bit-precision TFLOPS, 16x inflated vs. the 64-bit figure; GAAP/Wall-Street-'adjusted' earnings, a $1.7tn 'earnings illusion' once SBC dilution is properly normalised out) that's meaningless without a stricter, less flattering denominator. Neither page cites the other, and several of Burry's own 'Tragic Tier' SBC-abuse names (Palantir, CrowdStrike, Datadog, Marvell) are AI-infrastructure-adjacent companies the wiki elsewhere takes at face value. Concrete next step: cross-link the two pages' See Also sections. Separately, today's Finance portfolio-management-briefing data-integrity catch-up (unrelated to the focus-domain rotation, but new and concrete) surfaced a check_data_quality.py backlog of 804 non-'ok' rows, 106 of which are real, persistent 7-day yfinance-fetch failures on an EU-ticker cluster outside current holdings — distinct from and more actionable than the already-open 'script hung with zero output' thread from 2026-09-21. Concrete next step: pull the actual ticker list and check whether it's the same LSE/Euronext GLOBAL_QUOTE-vs-TIME_SERIES_DAILY quirk already fixed once for WOSG.L. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-21.
